name: System homomorphism is reflexive and transitive
description: Theorem 4.31: Z = HIMSY(Z, ID(SZ), ID(IZ), ID(OZ)) for every Z; and if Z1 = HIMSY(Z2, HS1, HI1, HO1) and Z2 = HIMSY(Z3, HS2, HI2, HO2) then Z1 = HIMSY(Z3, HS1∘HS2, HI1∘HI2, HO1∘HO2).

elements.text: The homomorphic-image relation is reflexive (identity homomorphisms) and transitive (componentwise composition).
Identity maps are surjective and trivially preserve NZ and RZ.
Composites of surjections are surjective; transition and readout consistency chain through the middle system.
